markdown_report:
The strongest initial direction remains a **receptive-field-aware recency diagnostic** for the supplied NextItNet. At 0% progress, establish implementation validity and characterize intervention sensitivity before adding architecture. Training-prefix effects alone cannot establish temporal generalization or predict validation gains.

### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors specific recent connections over broad similarity. Test recent-history dependence without treating inferred purpose, ownership, satisfaction, or compatibility as observed. (2) Existing probes measure embedding geometry and sampled margins. These cannot establish useful temporal dependence; missing valid samples must produce unavailable values, not healthy-looking zeros. (3) Left padding and causal convolutions determine historical coverage. Verify the actual backbone, padding behavior, and final-nonpadding readout before interpreting probes.

**Related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) uses residual dilated causal convolutions. Its maximum receptive-field span is `1 + Σ(k−1)d`, counting every convolution; exact reachable offsets depend on the dilation schedule. (2) The [perturbation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13165) motivates recency comparisons, but studies training-data removal. [Frozen-model shuffling](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.12008v1) measures order sensitivity; neither validates predictive usefulness on fitted prefixes. (3) [Sampled-evaluation research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) motivates broader ranking diagnostics. [Removal-explanation research](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/hash/1def1713ebf17722cbe300cfc1c88558-Abstract.html) additionally warns that replacement choices and unfamiliar inputs can dominate intervention effects.

### Framework and candidate directions

| Direction | Evidence | Gap addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation validity | Causality, exact reachable offsets, padding | Distinguish implementation faults from model limitations |
| Useful temporal dependence | Controlled interventions, fixed eligibility, target ranks | Separate measured sensitivity from evidence of generalization |
| Learning intervention | Preregistered diagnostic hypotheses and host validation | Test whether diagnosis supports improvement |

Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

1. **Paired recency probes — 5/7/5.** Originality: useful family-specific synthesis, but established perturbation methods. Potential: creates auditable evidence, but effects may reflect memorization or distribution shift. Difficulty: requires no retraining, but matching, exact ranks, and clustered uncertainty require substantial care. References: NextItNet; perturbation and removal-explanation studies.
2. **Recency-weighted next-item loss — 3/6/2.** Originality: direct diagnostic response, but familiar weighting. Potential: may prioritize recent transitions, but can discard useful older patterns. Difficulty: small loss change, but weighting needs validation. Define weights by target recency within each sampled training sequence, normalize over valid positions, and preregister strength; the perturbation study motivates testing rather than guarantees improvement.
3. **Learned gates on dilated residual blocks — 4/7/5.** Originality: integrates scale selection within NextItNet, but gating is established. Potential: permits adaptive historical coverage, but may overfit sparse histories. Difficulty: modest architecture change, but requires predictor and probe updates. Compute gates causally within the jointly trained network; retain one model per category. Reference: NextItNet.

### Selected algorithm: paired recency probes

Freeze each category’s single trained model. Deterministically sample training-prefix targets, excluding the target occurrence and all subsequent interactions from inputs. Label results **in-sample training diagnostics**: targets may have contributed to fitting, so strong ranks can reflect memorized transitions or popularity.

Retain the terminal history item and readout anchor. Compare recent versus older deletions inside actual reachable coverage, matching removal count and item-frequency strata; report lag differences because lag is the exposure of interest. For each targeted intervention, generate repeated random controls matched on count, lag bins, contiguous-run structure, and terminal handling. Report unmatched coverage. Deletion plus repacking changes adjacency, offsets, and receptive-field membership; record these changes rather than attributing effects solely to removed content.

```text
verify causality, padding behavior, reachable offsets, final-nonpadding readout
sample seeded training prefixes and fixed original-history candidate sets
for each eligible prefix and next-item target:
    create matched recent/older deletions and repeated random controls
    add full-window and terminal-preserving permutation controls
    repack and left-pad identically; encode each variant once
    stream catalog scores; record exact target ranks and sampled margins
    record top-10 overlap, positional shifts, coverage changes, and exclusions
bootstrap users within category; compute equal-weight macro effects
```

A secondary position-preserving replacement probe can distinguish structural compression from content alteration only partially. Use the same documented replacement rule for targeted and random controls; report induced distribution shift. Interior PAD is not ordinary left padding, zero embeddings need not yield zero intermediate activations, and a new untrained mask token is unsuitable. Inspect actual masking before enabling this probe.

Freeze eligibility from each original prefix: exclude padding and observed items, retaining the target exactly once. Flag repeated targets and report repeat/nonrepeat, prefix-length, target-popularity, and training-transition-frequency strata. Keep simulator unseen-item eligibility separate. Compute exact rank as `1 + count(score > target_score) + count(score == target_score and item_id < target_id)`; validate chunked scoring against exhaustive sorting on tiny cases covering ties, repeats, padding, and chunk boundaries. Use the same tie rule for top-10 overlap.

Report paired changes, denominators, matching coverage, and seeded 95% user-cluster bootstrap intervals, preserving all observations per sampled user. Average prefixes within users before category means; bootstrap categories independently before their equal-weight macro average. Fix and record prefix caps, intervention sizes, lag bins, control repetitions, replacement rules, and bootstrap repetitions before execution. Count diagnostics toward the shared GPU budget and report their cost.

Treat findings as sensitivity evidence, not validation gains. Preregister a minimal subsequent intervention and its predicted direction; select using unchanged host macro validation HR@10. Diagnostic usefulness requires corroboration across independently trained trials and out-of-sample prediction of gains; exploratory correlation is insufficient. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt`, and all ModelView hooks. Return measured metrics, definitions, sample counts, and explicit unavailable values; category metadata lists remain empty. Keep four-category routing, supplied seeds and limits, one model/checkpoint per category, and matching predictor writer. Never infer unavailable reviews or simulator traits.

idea.description: Strengthen the NextItNet diagnostic adapter with controlled recency interventions, fixed candidate eligibility, exact chunked target ranks, and user-cluster uncertainty. Interpret training-prefix measurements as intervention sensitivity rather than evidence of generalization.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests recent specific interests receive insufficient attention, while existing embedding and sampled-margin probes cannot establish useful temporal dependence. The revised protocol addresses deletion-induced temporal compression, replacement artifacts, memorized transitions, candidate-set confounding, and unstable tie handling before proposing a training change.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the corrected NextItNet cold start and one independently trained checkpoint per category. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Compute receptive-field span from every convolution and exact reachable offsets from the actual architecture; inspect normalization, biases, masking, causality, and padding effects. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and ModelView interfaces including log2feats(sequence), item_emb, and predict_score(features, items). The loader contract remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Use training prefixes only, excluding the target occurrence and subsequent interactions from inputs; explicitly label target ranks as in-sample diagnostics. Retain the terminal item, gather the actual final nonpadding index, and exclude empty histories with counts. Freeze original-prefix candidate eligibility across variants, retain the target exactly once, and flag repeated targets. Separate simulator full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the prescribed twenty training users from diagnostic eligibility. Use no unavailable review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores, or inferred simulator traits. Return empty category breakdowns and explicit unavailable values when evidence is absent. Before running, record deterministic prefix sampling and caps, intervention sizes, lag bins, frequency strata, control repetitions, bootstrap repetitions, and replacement rules. Match recent/older deletion sets by count and frequency strata; match each intervention's random controls additionally by lag and contiguous-run structure. Report matching failures, positional shifts, and changes in reachable membership. Replacement probes are optional and require implementation-specific padding checks; never introduce an untrained mask token. Encode each variant once and stream exact catalog ranks using ascending item ID to break score ties. Validate against exhaustive sorting on small synthetic cases. Average prefix effects within users, then users within categories; bootstrap users within category and compute the four-category macro average. Record diagnostic GPU cost against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Keep the pinned host validation evaluator authoritative. No initial model change is required; any later architecture change must update the embedded predictor writer and retain a single jointly trained NextItNet network.
idea.pseudocode:
Set and record diagnostic seed 42 and all protocol parameters before execution.
For each category's frozen single NextItNet:
  Verify causal behavior, actual reachable offsets, padding effects, and final-nonpadding readout.
  Deterministically sample training-prefix/next-training-item examples.
  Exclude empty or unmatched examples with explicit counts.
  For each example:
    Fix eligible catalog IDs from the original prefix; exclude PAD and observed IDs except the target.
    Retain the target exactly once and flag whether it repeats a historical item.
    Construct recent and older deletion sets matched by count and frequency strata.
    Retain the terminal item; construct repeated random controls matched to each intervention.
    Add full-window and terminal-preserving permutations with identical targets and candidates.
    If padding behavior supports a documented replacement probe, add matched replacement controls.
    Repack deletion histories and left-pad consistently.
    Record retained-token position shifts and changes in structural reachable membership.
    Encode each history once via log2feats; gather its final nonpadding feature.
    Score the target and stream eligible item chunks via predict_score.
    Accumulate rank = 1 + greater-score count + tied-score/lower-ID count.
    Record paired ranks, diagnostic HR@10, sampled margins, and deterministic top-10 overlap.
  Validate chunked rank implementation against exhaustive sorting on tiny controlled examples.
  Stratify effects by prefix length, target popularity, transition frequency, and repeated targets.
  Average prefix effects within each user, then average users within category.
Resample users with replacement independently within categories, preserving paired observations.
Recompute category effects and equal-weight macro effects for seeded 95% intervals.
Return metrics, metric_definitions, coverage, sample counts, unavailable values, and GPU cost.
Generate an interpretation prompt distinguishing measured sensitivity from generalization hypotheses.
Preregister any subsequent single-model intervention and assess it with unchanged host validation.

originality.positive: Combines architectural reachability, compression controls, fixed eligibility, and exact ranking into a reproducible family-specific diagnostic.
originality.negative: The constituent perturbation, ranking, and bootstrap techniques are established; originality lies in their integration.

future_potential.positive: Can expose implementation faults and guide minimal, testable NextItNet interventions across all four categories.
future_potential.negative: In-sample sensitivity may reflect memorization or unfamiliar inputs, and its ability to predict validation gains remains unmeasured.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the frozen network and existing feature and scoring hooks without fitting additional predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact reachability checks, intervention matching, deterministic catalog ranking, coverage accounting, and clustered uncertainty require more work than a simple probe extension.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Introduces residual dilated causal convolutions for next-item recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for causality and receptive-field checks.
limitations: Does not establish that temporal perturbation sensitivity identifies current intent or predicts improvement on this benchmark.
Maximum receptive-field span alone does not describe every reachable offset.

related_work.title: Interaction-position perturbation study
contributions: The supplied research summary reports stronger effects from removing recent training interactions.
limitations: Training-data removal differs from inference-time intervention on a frozen model.
Does not justify attributing compacted-deletion effects solely to removed content.

related_work.title: Hidasi and Czapp: recommender evaluation flaws
contributions: Documents evaluation problems involving negative sampling.
Supports corroborating sampled margins with broader ranking diagnostics.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed probes or authorize changing the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Hase et al.: removal-based explanations and out-of-distribution behavior
contributions: Shows that removal-based explanations can be affected by unfamiliar inputs and replacement choices.
Motivates matched controls and explicit limits on causal interpretation.
limitations: Does not directly validate the proposed NextItNet replacement or deletion protocol.

related_work.title: Klenitskiy et al.: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Studies frozen-model sensitivity to shuffled histories using accuracy and ranking overlap.
Motivates separating terminal-item dependence from broader order sensitivity.
limitations: Applying the approach to fitted training prefixes cannot establish temporal generalization.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes discrepancies between sampled and full-catalog recommendation metrics.
Supports treating full-catalog diagnostics and benchmark sampled HR@10 as distinct quantities.
limitations: Does not establish that full-catalog intervention effects predict gains under the pinned sampled evaluator.

related_work.title: Cluster bootstrap reference
contributions: Supports resampling clustered observations together to preserve within-cluster dependence.
Motivates user-level resampling with paired prefixes retained.
limitations: Bootstrap intervals do not correct intervention distribution shift, selection bias, or in-sample memorization.
